newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Kato expects to go public by year-end - Kamel.
newsitem.headline: Kato expects to go public by year-end - Kamel.

text.p: The chairman of Egypt's Kato group of companies said on Monday he was consolidating his interests into a holding company in preparation for going public later this year.
Chairman Ibrahim Kamel said he was willing to sell off more than 50 percent of the holding company through the Egyptian stock exchange but he would remain the largest shareholder.

"I would be very happy to put at least 50 percent of the company on the stock exchange. I wouldn't mind giving up the absolute majority," Kamel told Reuters in the Swiss resort of Davos, where he is attending the World Economic Forum.

The Kato group of companies has interests in the food, soap and fragrance industries, real estate, banking, tourism and most recently in aviation. It is based in Cairo but it also has operations in France, the United States, Uganda and Albania.
Kamel said he had not gone public in the past because the Egyptian stock exchange was so quiet but this had changed with the sudden boom in stock market activity.
"What we intend to do is to complete putting the present holdings under the umbrella of one holding comany so that when we go public it will be much easier.

"Already the beginning of it (the holding company) is Kato Investments and before the end of 1997 we should have completed our task. I would say by the end of 1997 we will be among the first (closed Egyptian companies) to go public," he added.
Kamel said it was too early to say what level of market capitalisation Kato Investments could expect.
